text:
amy.w: Hey team, I have a customer report for a failed inference that gives trace_id=ab12cd34ef but I can't find a matching request_id in our ELK logs. Any tips on correlating traces -> raw access logs when the request_id seems to be dropped by a proxy? :thinking:

ben.k: Did you check the ingest proxy hop? Sometimes Envoy strips x-request-id unless nginx sets it. Which region and service?

amy.w: us-west-2, service=redwood-runtime-prod. Trace is in Honeycomb, spans show ingress -> runtime -> model but the runtime spans have no request_id tag. Hop before runtime shows header x-ctx-id with same hex as trace id.

cj: Two quick options: 1) lookup trace in Honeycomb and copy span.event.trace_hex and search our nginx logs for that hex as a substring (we sometimes propagate trace id in x-ctx-id). 2) if you have a span.timestamp, grep S3 raw logs around that minute.

amy.w: Can you paste the exact commands you use? I'm on my laptop with AWS access.

cj: Sure. In Honeycomb open the trace, copy the trace id (ab12cd34ef). Try first: 

```bash
# search recent nginx objects in S3 (gzipped) for the trace id 
aws s3 cp s3://prod-logs/nginx/$(date -u +%Y/%m/%d)/ - | zgrep -i ab12cd34ef || true
```

Or via our CLI that queries structured logs: 

```bash
redwoodctl logs query --env prod --service runtime --filter "message:ab12cd34ef OR headers.x-ctx-id:ab12cd34ef" --since "15m"
```

ben.k: If that yields nothing, check the ingress proxy config: we had a rollout a week ago that normalized `x-request-id` -> `x-ctx-id`. Sometimes the header name changed and our log parser only reads x-request-id. Quick workaround is to run the parser locally with fallback header list: 

```python
# small snippet to parse fallback headers
def get_req_id(headers):
    return headers.get('x-request-id') or headers.get('x-ctx-id') or headers.get('x-redwood-id')
```

amy.w: ran the redwoodctl query, found one line in runtime stdout with headers.x-ctx-id=ab12cd34ef but no request_id field. There's a request line showing upstream 10.2.3.4:5044 -> 502.

observability-bot: FYI: dashboard link for runtime access logs: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rtg123/runtime-access-logs?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2

amy.w: Nice. Any guidance for alert tuning? We keep getting page noise when proxies return 502s during small rolling deploys.

infra-oncall: For alert tuning, reduce sensitivity of the 5xx rate alert on runtime-prod by adding a rollback window: require sustained >2% 5xx for 5m across >=2 hosts before paging. Also add a tag filter to ignore status=502 when reason contains "upstream_unavailable". I can open the alert PR if you'd like.

amy.w: Please do the PR. For my immediate work I'll correlate trace->raw line and attach request snippet to the bug. Thanks! :thumbsup:

ben.k: One last tip — if you need to rehydrate full request body, use the replay key from the span (if present) and run: 

```bash
redwoodctl replay fetch --trace ab12cd34ef --output ./replay.json
```

amy.w: That returned the request headers. Saved. Will attach to the ticket and close this loop. Thanks all.

cj: Awesome, glad you found it. If the proxy is trimming x-request-id we'll plan a small fix to normalize headers at the edge so logs and traces correlate automatically.

amy.w: Adding follow-up: can someone add a short runbook snippet for this pattern to the observability docs? I'll create a PR tomorrow.
